# 1. Packages

Install once (run in the console), then load every time.

```{r packages, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("quantmod", "TTR", "ggplot2", "knitr", "rmarkdown"))
```

```{r libraries}
library(quantmod)  # download and chart financial data
library(TTR)       # technical trading rules (SMA, etc.)
```

# 2. Configuration

The portfolio is read from `portfolio.txt` (one symbol per line).

```{r config}
portfolio_file <- "portfolio.txt"
start_date     <- as.Date("2023-01-01")
end_date       <- Sys.Date()
ma_window      <- 20   # moving average window (trading days)
```

# 3. Function: load_stock_data()

Reads the symbols from the text file and imports the data of each one with
`quantmod::getSymbols()`. Returns a named list with one data frame per symbol.
A symbol that fails to download is reported and skipped, so one bad ticker does
not stop the rest.

```{r load-function}
load_stock_data <- function(file = portfolio_file,
                            from = start_date,
                            to   = end_date) {
  if (!file.exists(file)) stop("File not found: ", file)

  symbols <- trimws(readLines(file, warn = FALSE))
  symbols <- unique(toupper(symbols[symbols != ""]))

  stocks <- list()
  for (sym in symbols) {
    xts_data <- tryCatch(
      getSymbols(sym, src = "yahoo", from = from, to = to, auto.assign = FALSE),
      error = function(e) {
        message("Could not download ", sym, ": ", conditionMessage(e))
        NULL
      }
    )
    if (is.null(xts_data)) next

    df <- data.frame(Date = index(xts_data), coredata(xts_data))
    colnames(df) <- c("Date", "Open", "High", "Low", "Close", "Volume", "Adjusted")
    stocks[[sym]] <- df
  }
  stocks
}
```

```{r load-data}
stocks <- load_stock_data()
names(stocks)
```

# 4. Function: calculate_statistics()

Takes one stock data frame and returns the requested statistics on the closing
price: moving average, mean, mode, median and standard deviation.

R has no built-in statistical mode (`mode()` returns the object type), so a
small helper is defined. Prices are rounded to 2 decimals so repeated values
can be found.

```{r stats-function}
get_mode <- function(x) {
  x  <- round(x, 2)
  ux <- unique(x)
  ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]
}

calculate_statistics <- function(df, window = ma_window) {
  close <- df$Close
  ma    <- SMA(close, n = window)

  list(
    summary = data.frame(
      Mean              = mean(close, na.rm = TRUE),
      Median            = median(close, na.rm = TRUE),
      Mode              = get_mode(close),
      StdDev            = sd(close, na.rm = TRUE),
      Latest_MovingAvg  = tail(ma[!is.na(ma)], 1),
      Observations      = length(close)
    ),
    moving_average = data.frame(Date = df$Date, Close = close, MA = ma)
  )
}
```

```{r compute-stats}
stats <- lapply(stocks, calculate_statistics)

# One summary table with a row per stock
stats_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(stats), function(s) {
  cbind(Symbol = s, stats[[s]]$summary)
}))
rownames(stats_table) <- NULL
stats_table[, -1] <- round(stats_table[, -1], 2)
stats_table
```

# 5. Display utilities

Several ways of presenting the same data, similar to Yahoo Finance.

```{r display-functions}
# (a) First and last rows of each stock's data frame
display_data_frames <- function(stocks, n = 5) {
  for (sym in names(stocks)) {
    cat("\n=====", sym, "=====\n")
    cat("Rows:", nrow(stocks[[sym]]), "| From:", as.character(min(stocks[[sym]]$Date)),
        "To:", as.character(max(stocks[[sym]]$Date)), "\n")
    print(head(stocks[[sym]], n))
    cat("...\n")
    print(tail(stocks[[sym]], n))
  }
}

# (b) Quote summary: latest price, daily change, 52-week range
display_quote_summary <- function(stocks) {
  rows <- lapply(names(stocks), function(sym) {
    d      <- stocks[[sym]]
    last   <- tail(d, 1)
    prev   <- tail(d, 2)[1, ]
    last52 <- d[d$Date >= (max(d$Date) - 365), ]
    data.frame(
      Symbol     = sym,
      Last       = round(last$Close, 2),
      Change     = round(last$Close - prev$Close, 2),
      Change_Pct = round((last$Close / prev$Close - 1) * 100, 2),
      Low_52w    = round(min(last52$Low), 2),
      High_52w   = round(max(last52$High), 2),
      Volume     = last$Volume
    )
  })
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}

# (c) Price chart with moving average for one stock
plot_price_ma <- function(sym) {
  m <- stats[[sym]]$moving_average
  plot(m$Date, m$Close, type = "l", col = "steelblue", lwd = 1.5,
       xlab = "Date", ylab = "Close price (USD)",
       main = paste0(sym, " - Close and ", ma_window, "-day moving average"))
  lines(m$Date, m$MA, col = "firebrick", lwd = 2)
  legend("topleft", legend = c("Close", paste0(ma_window, "-day MA")),
         col = c("steelblue", "firebrick"), lwd = c(1.5, 2), bty = "n")
}

# (d) Candlestick chart with volume (quantmod)
plot_candlestick <- function(sym, last_days = 90) {
  d   <- tail(stocks[[sym]], last_days)
  x   <- xts::xts(d[, c("Open", "High", "Low", "Close", "Volume", "Adjusted")],
                  order.by = d$Date)
  chartSeries(x, name = paste(sym, "- last", last_days, "days"),
              type = "candlesticks", theme = chartTheme("white"),
              TA = "addVo();addSMA(n=20)")
}

# (e) Histogram of closing prices with mean and median
plot_histogram <- function(sym) {
  close <- stocks[[sym]]$Close
  hist(close, breaks = 30, col = "lightgray", border = "white",
       main = paste(sym, "- Distribution of closing prices"),
       xlab = "Close price (USD)")
  abline(v = mean(close),   col = "firebrick", lwd = 2)
  abline(v = median(close), col = "steelblue", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
  legend("topright", legend = c("Mean", "Median"),
         col = c("firebrick", "steelblue"), lwd = 2, lty = c(1, 2), bty = "n")
}
```

```

```

```{r plot-compare, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}

        main = "Mean closing price by stock", ylab = "USD")
```
